purpose: library: big-O notation — the informal and formal definitions (f(n) = O(g(n)) means positive constants c and k exist with 0 ≤ f(n) ≤ cg(n) for all n ≥ k), the worked example n² + 3n + 4 is O(n²) because n² + 3n + 4 < 2n² for all n > 10, the Θ versus O distinction, and the worked quicksort-versus-bubble-sort comparison for 1,000,000 numbers (20,000,000 steps on average versus 1,000,000,000,000). Fits quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the step counts, a compare table of O/Θ/Ω notations, and a formula explorer for the inequality.
